howItWorks.title: An old idea, built for today
howItWorks.intro: IGUDAR is named after the igudar, the collective granaries of the Amazigh. The same four ideas hold up the platform.

building.title: One shared building
building.story: The igudar were the Amazigh collective granaries: one strong building that many families raised and guarded together.
building.inIgudar: A property bought through IGUDAR works the same way. One building, many owners.

chamber.title: Your own chamber
chamber.story: Each family kept its own chamber, marked and remembered.
chamber.inIgudar: You hold shares of the company that owns the property, a defined and recorded part, never an unwritten promise.

keeper.title: A trusted keeper
keeper.story: A granary needed a keeper everyone trusted.
keeper.inIgudar: Here, a regulated bank holds your money in escrow, and a professional operator rents and looks after the property.

rules.title: Rules written down
rules.story: Everyone agreed the rules before the first harvest.
rules.inIgudar: Ours are written in the shareholders' agreement, and the fee grid is published in full, the same for everyone.

follow.title: Follow every dirham
follow.body: Your wallet shows four things: what you committed, what sits in escrow, what is invested in the property company, and the rent you have actually received. Nothing hidden, nothing to guess.

moneyMoves.intro: Your money is never mixed with ours. It waits in an escrow account until the raise succeeds, and goes back to you in full if it does not.

steps.transfer: You transfer your amount from your own bank account to an escrow account at a regulated bank, one account per project.
steps.close: If the raise reaches its target, the property company (SAS) buys the property. If it fails or the deadline passes, the bank refunds you in full.
steps.lease: The property is rented to a professional operator under a master lease.
steps.rent: Rent first pays the reserve, taxes and the platform fee. What is left is paid to your bank account as a net distribution.
steps.exit: Exit windows open every {months} months after the first year. The property is sold, or sold in a block, around year {holdYears}, and you get your capital back plus or minus the change in the property value.
